title: Reentrant localization transition, quantum butterfly and robust edge modes in aperiodic zig-zag ladder
authors: Sayan Bhattacharya, Rhiddha Acharjee, Atanu Nandy
abstract: Low dimensional tight-binding lattices in presence of quasiperiodic disorder generally exhibits localization transition. The system supports diffusive modes upto a limiting strength of disorder and all the eigenstates become localized beyond that critical strength thereby quenching the kinetic signature of the wavepacket. However, moving away from this situation, we demonstrate that with minimal long-range off-diagonal modulation, the eigenspectrum again may offer delocalization of electronic states for some subtle combination of kinetic parameters of the Hamiltonian leading to a second quantum phase change. The localization transitions are associated with the obvious presence of single-particle mobility edges. Multifractal energy landscape also shows quantum butterfly pattern with the in-gap robust edge modes. The re-emerging localization transition is manifested through the evaluation of inverse participation ratio, eigenspectrum and a pertinent quantum dynamical study.
summary: This work analyzes a quasiperiodic zig-zag ladder model to reveal a reentrant localization transition driven by kinetic parameter tuning. Using advanced diagnostics like IPR and multifractal analysis, the authors demonstrate that delocalized states can reappear in regimes previously thought localized. Furthermore, they identify robust edge modes whose existence is mapped onto the system's quantum butterfly spectrum.
main_problem: The study investigates reentrant localization transitions, quantum butterfly patterns, and robust edge modes in quasiperiodic lattices.
main_result: The system exhibits a re-emerging delocalization phase controlled by kinetic parameters, alongside the formation of robust edge states resistant to moderate disorder.
method: Analysis employs diagnostics like Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), Mean Square Displacement (MSD) scaling ($	ext{MSD} \sim t^\mu$), and multifractal analysis ($I_q$) across phase diagrams.
model_or_system: The model is a quasi-one dimensional zig-zag ladder network governed by a tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating a quasiperiodic Aubry-Andre Harper (AAH) modulation in the long-range hopping integral.
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio ($	ext{IPR}_n$), Normalized Participation Ratio ($	ext{NPR}_n$), transport exponent ($\mu$), edge probability ($P_{	ext{edge}}$), and the phase diagram parameter $\eta$.
important_parameters: The slowness index ($\alpha$) controls the transition, alongside the ratio of hopping strengths ($t/\lambda_0$) and disorder strength ($W_d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of multifractal scaling techniques for characterizing quantum phases in quasiperiodic systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate IPR intensity plots showing delocalized patches, MSD vs. time curves demonstrating different transport regimes ($\mu$), and maps correlating edge probability onto the quantum butterfly spectrum.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes localization diagnostics (IPR/NPR) to map out a reentrant phase diagram controlled by $\alpha$, followed by dynamical studies using MSD and multifractal analysis, culminating in the identification of robust edge modes via $P_{	ext{edge}}$ mapping onto the spectrum.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed diagnostics (IPR, multifractals, dynamics) for understanding how subtle changes in Hamiltonian parameters can induce complex phase transitions (re-entrant localization) beyond simple disorder effects, which is relevant to engineered quantum materials.
